//: step-ca configuration. This file is the source of truth: scripts/deploy.sh
pushes it, and it must never be edited on pistis.
authority.enableAdmin is false on purpose. With it true, provisioners move
into the badger DB and `step ca provisioner add` becomes the only way to
change them - which would quietly make this file a lie.
The JWK provisioner slot below is filled in by deploy.sh from secrets.env.
It is minted once on first deploy and kept there: re-minting would change
the kid on every run and invalidate anyone's bootstrapped client config.

crl.//: Serves the leaf CRL at /1.0/crl. The CRL named in the G3 certificate itself is the *root's*, published as a static file by nginx.

claims.//: Applies to the JWK provisioner: 30 days by default, a year at most, for things that cannot do ACME.

//: One provisioner offering all three challenge types: http-01 for hosts
with a reachable port 80, tls-alpn-01 for port 443, dns-01 for hosts
dns-01 needs no credentials on this side - step-ca only *reads* the
_acme-challenge TXT record. It is the ACME client that needs the
PowerDNS API key to write it into the home. zone on Pythia; that key
Lifetimes are deliberately Let's Encrypt shaped. Anything on ACME
renews unattended, so a long lifetime buys nothing and costs you a
provisioners.name: acme
